title: Session lease RBAC gate and KMS usage quarantine
author: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: Adds a lightweight session-lease enforcement layer to the RBAC v2 decision path and a KMS usage quarantine policy that temporarily isolates keys used by sessions whose residency or consent signals are ambiguous.

Motivation: We observed two classes of risky behavior in production: (1) long-lived delegated operator sessions that outlive intended short leases, widening blast radius when operator credentials are stolen; (2) intermittent KMS requests that lacked clear residency or consent metadata and therefore could be routed to the wrong region. This PR implements a policy gate that enforces session TTLs at the policy-evaluator level and tags KMS requests for quarantine until residency/consent is confirmed.

Design:
- Session lease enforcer: a middleware in the RBAC v2 evaluator that checks 'session_lease_expires_at' on operator claims and rejects or flags requests where the lease has expired. Supports a transparent renewal hint flow for SDKs to surface a 412-ish signal to callers.
- KMS quarantine: KMS client interceptor that writes an audit-quarantine tag and routes the request to a holding queue for short-circuit validation (residency check, consent cache lookup). If validation completes within the configured grace window (default 5s) the request is forwarded; otherwise the request is rejected with a clear error and audit entry.
- Metrics and tracing: new counters and histograms (security.session_lease.rejects, security.kms.quarantine.duration_ms) plus trace annotations to link the original request to quarantine evaluation.
- Config: per-tenant defaults with operator override guardrails; global feature flag 'session_lease_enforcer_v1' for staged rollout.

Backwards compatibility: If the feature flag is off, behavior is identical to today.

Release notes:
- Security: enforce session leases and introduce KMS quarantine path to prevent ambiguous-region KMS ops. New errors: SESSION_LEASE_EXPIRED, KMS_QUARANTINED.

Migration notes: tenants with long-lived operator sessions should migrate to issued session leases or opt-in to a gradual migration flow.
